name: Cereal Rye (Stooling Rye)
harvestProduct: winter grazing/fodder/silage and green-manure biomass, killed at early boot stage before summer grain planting

evidence.quote: Once well-established, it can withstand very cold conditions (down to -35°C).
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 19: Stooling rye, SA Grain/Grain SA (Truter, Dannhauser, Smith & Trytsman), 2019

evidence.quote: The best time to seed this species is February/March.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 19: Stooling rye, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: The best time to seed this species is February/March.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 19: Stooling rye, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: It is recommended to harvest rye no later than at early boot stage (before heading) in order to maintain good palatability, intake and nutritive value.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 19: Stooling rye, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: It is used as a cover crop and killed two weeks before planting summer grain.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 19: Stooling rye, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

daysToHarvestRange.notes: Termination is defined by growth stage (early boot) and by proximity to the following summer-grain planting date, not by a day-count from sowing.

evidence.quote: Seeding rates can be between 25 kg/ha – 50 kg/ha (dryland) and 50 kg/ha – 75 kg/ha (irrigated) and depends upon whether it is sown in a mixture or not.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 19: Stooling rye, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

yield.product: dry matter (fodder/green-manure biomass) at boot stage

evidence.quote: When the plant reaches boot stage, the species should yield in the order of 7 tons – 10 tons of dry matter (DM)/ha under optimal management conditions.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 19: Stooling rye, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: It is used as a cover crop and killed two weeks before planting summer grain.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 19: Stooling rye, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

zoneNotes.highveld: Grown in areas with cold winters/warm dry summers; tolerates -35°C once established; sown Feb/March ahead of winter grazing and killed before the next summer grain crop.
zoneNotes.karoo-arid: Relatively drought-resistant, can tolerate annual rainfall as low as 400mm.

gaps: No row/in-row spacing or sow-depth figures found (this cereal is drilled/broadcast, not spaced as a row crop in the source).
No explicit days-to-harvest day-count; only growth-stage (early boot) and calendar-relative (two weeks before summer grain) termination cues.
No named SA rye cultivars found (source mentions diploid vs tetraploid cultivars generically without naming SA-marketed ones).
summary: Sow window (Feb/Mar), seed rate (25-75 kg/ha dryland/irrigated) and DM biomass yield at boot stage (7-10 t/ha) are all directly sourced from Grain SA's Part 19 (Stooling rye) article. Not a legume, so N-fixed is null. Spacing and an exact days-to-termination figure are gaps; termination is described only by growth stage and by proximity to the next planting.
